name: Schenklengsfelder Dorflinde
age_estimate: widely disputed, roughly 600-1300 years; a stone inscription claims a planting date of 760 CE

location.address: Marktplatz / Straße an der Linde, Schenklengsfeld, Landkreis Hersfeld-Rotenburg

access: Free, public market square in the village centre.
transport: Not verified; no confirmed public transport stop found. Schenklengsfeld is roughly 10km southeast of Bad Hersfeld, Hessen; reachable by car or regional bus, no rail station in the village.
verify_notes: Single-tree-destination exception (2026-08-31 ruling), and one of the strongest candidates found in this whole batch: sources describe it as possibly Germany's oldest deciduous tree and the tree with the largest trunk circumference in the country. Girth 17.91m (measured 15 July 2007, both sources agree), height only about 10m (the crown itself has been reduced over centuries); the tree is now four separate vital trunk sections around the rim of what was once a single stem, carried by an 80-beam, roughly 65m wooden support scaffold that is itself a remarkable sight. Naturdenkmal, protected since the 1920s-30s under successive German nature-conservation laws, with major restoration work in 1976, 2009 and 2020; the fire department watered it with 100,000 litres during the 2018 heatwave, evidence of active civic care. AGE: genuinely unsettled and should be presented as such rather than resolved. A stone marker (added in the 20th century) claims planting in 760 CE (roughly 1270 years); published dendrology estimates range from 600 to 1300+ years depending on the author (Froehlich 1990: over 1000 years; Lenzing 2005: 1200-1300 years; other literature: 600-1000 years). Do not pick a winner; state the range and note the marker's claim is folklore-adjacent rather than dated proof. History: served as an official Gerichtslinde (court tree) continuously 1557-1796 and intermittently after, plus a market and dance site with a pillory once nearby; still hosts a biennial Lindenbluetenfest (lime-blossom festival). Coordinates from the two sources agree closely, tree-level confirmed. Alive and vital per baumkunde's most recent visit (27 October 2022).
